Subject: Post-call recap: retention & logs (next steps)

Thanks for your time today, Danielle — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side. Appreciate the thoughtful questions on retention/backups and how Redwood handles deletion requests for customer data.

Key notes from the call:
- Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for our hosted API; Private deployments can be integrated with customer KMS and audit hooks.
- We retain operational logs for 90 days by default; platform-level access logs (auth/route) are retained for 365 days with an option for Extended Log Retention add-on.
- Backups: snapshots for model-serving nodes are taken nightly; customer data snapshots are retained for 30 days unless otherwise configured.
- Deletion flow: we support both on-demand erasure via API (subject to propagation windows) and scheduled purge jobs; RPO/RTO vary by deployment type.

Proposed next actions:
1) Ill send a short vendor questionnaire for your security team to complete (attached) — can we target EOD next Tuesday for the questionnaire?
2) Rachel / Monica will prepare a one-page SOC 2 summary and the retention matrix so you can share with legal/compliance.
3) If helpful, schedule a focused Ops session to review retention timelines and backup custody (30 min).

Danielle — please flag anything I missed or correct any dates.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Danielle — answering your questions below and attaching the SOC 2 one-pager + preliminary retention matrix. See inline: 

1) 365-day access logs: for Hosted customers logs are encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys by default. For Private deployments we offer integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) so keys are customer-managed and we can surface key rotation records in the audit trail.

2) Deletion propagation window for hosted customers: we surface "deletion accepted" immediately in the API. For irreversible removal from backups/snapshots the upper bound is 30 days — that is, backups containing the data may persist in snapshot retention windows for up to 30 days before final purge. We do offer an Erasure Acceleration service (enterprise add-on) that shortens this to 7 days in scoped cases; this requires an advance contractual commitment.

3) Backups: all backups are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. For hosted customers, encryption keys are Redwood-managed unless the customer purchases Dedicated/Private and configures their own KMS. We also maintain a snapshot metadata log that records snapshot creation time, retention window, and operator ID (internal). That metadata is included in SOC 2 evidence packages.

Attached: SOC2-summary.pdf, data-retention-matrix.csv (prelim). Ive left a couple of cells blank in the matrix where we need information on your target erase window for specific data classes.

If youd like the Ops deep-dive, Monica and I are available next Wed (6/3) 10:00-10:30 PT — Ben, can you coordinate if that works for LumaHealth?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
